provenance: Domain names, weightings and scoring format are taken from Anthropic's own public certification listing (Anthropic Academy / Skilljar). Every question, explanation, analogy and cheat sheet in this app is original, community-authored practice content written against those published domains and the linked course material — it is not sourced from, and does not reproduce, any real exam item. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic.

scaled_score.note: Anthropic reports results on a 100-1000 scale; 720 is ~72%, which is what this app tracks internally.

scoring: Multiple choice and multiple response. Multi-response items require every correct option and no incorrect one — there is no partial credit.

domains.name: Agentic Architecture & Orchestration
objectives: Design subagents with correctly scoped tools, models and isolation boundaries
Choose between a skill, a subagent, a hook and plain memory for a given requirement
Build agent applications on the Claude Agent SDK: query() vs a persistent client, custom in-process tools, permission callbacks
Orchestrate multi-agent fan-out/reduce and reason about its cost and context trade-offs
Externalise state for long-running agent loops and bound runaway iteration
Place human-approval gates where reversibility is low and cost of a wrong action is high

domains.name: Tool Design & MCP Integration
objectives: Explain MCP architecture: host, client, server, and the tools/resources/prompts primitive split
Choose a transport (stdio vs Streamable HTTP) and a server scope (local, project, user)
Author well-specified tools: narrow verbs, clear descriptions and schemas, server-side validation
Secure MCP servers: authentication, per-caller authorisation, least-privileged credentials, confused-deputy avoidance
Decide when a capability belongs in an MCP server versus a skill, a hook or a plain permission rule
Debug MCP connection failures and tool-name or tool-selection collisions

domains.name: Claude Code Configuration & Workflows
objectives: Reason about settings precedence: enterprise managed policy, CLI flags, project and user settings
Configure the permission system: allow/ask/deny rules, permission modes, least-privileged tool grants
Run Claude Code headlessly for CI/CD with deterministic, parseable output and bounded turns
Design safe automation: idempotent jobs, scoped credentials, fork-PR safety, fail-closed pipelines
Operate sessions: continue/resume, compaction, rewind, slash commands and their frontmatter
Deploy at enterprise scale via Bedrock/Vertex/a gateway, with telemetry and audit in place

domains.name: Prompt Engineering & Structured Output
objectives: Apply core prompting technique: role framing, XML/structured delimiting, few-shot examples, chain of thought
Produce reliable structured output: schema-first prompting, prefilling, grounding against fabrication
Select a model tier against latency, cost and capability requirements for a given workload
Use extended thinking budgets where deliberation changes the outcome, and not where it doesn't
Apply prompt caching and batch processing correctly, including cache-ordering and break-even reasoning
Forecast and control token spend across a team or workload

domains.name: Context Management & Reliability
objectives: Design CLAUDE.md hierarchies and apply progressive disclosure to control context cost
Diagnose context exhaustion and choose between compaction, clearing and externalised state
Mitigate prompt injection: treat tool output as data, remove valuable targets, gate outbound actions
Apply defence-in-depth for autonomous or unattended agents: containment, egress control, audit trails
Verify agent output mechanically (tests, diffs) rather than trusting a self-report
Maintain memory and configuration as living artefacts that are reviewed like code

question_types.single: One correct answer of four or five options.
question_types.multi: Two or three correct answers; the stem states how many to select.
